subject: Proposed CLA + Hosting SLA for OpenWeights Consortium models
messages:
From: Dr. Lena Voss <lena@openweights.org>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ScaleFabric Ltd (legal) <legal@scalefabric.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential hosting & distribution terms for OpenWeights models

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The Consortium is interested in a hosting arrangement that preserves our upstream license terms but lets trusted partners (like Redwood) serve model weights and provide hosted inference under a concise contributor/hosting license.

Attached is a brief CLA draft (OW-CLA-draft.docx) and a one-page outline of hosting expectations. High-level asks from our side:
- OpenWeights retains copyright and original model metadata.
- Hosting partner must enforce no-retraining-for-proprietary-derivatives clause unless separately agreed.
- Clear attribution and provenance headers on requests that surface model names.
- Quarterly usage reporting back to OW for research attribution.
- Revenue share or hosting fee model to be discussed.

We are flexible on SLA and pricing; want to make sure the CLA doesn't block Redwood from offering hosted API products. Happy to loop in legal (ScaleFabric) for redlines.

Best,
Lena
Dr. Lena Voss
OpenWeights Consortium — Partnerships

Attachment: OW-CLA-draft.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Dr. Lena Voss <lena@openweights.org>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential hosting & distribution terms for OpenWeights models

Lena —

Really appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft. High-level reaction from our side:
- We can accept retention of upstream copyright and provenance headers. That maps well to our model catalog metadata pipeline.
- The restriction on retraining for proprietary derivatives is workable but we'd ask for an exception to allow Redwood to host customer fine-tuned checkpoints that are solely customer-owned (we'd require a separate opt-in under customer contracts).
- Reporting: quarterly usage is fine; we can push an anonymized telemetry feed and an aggregated usage report.
- For pricing: Redwood prefers a hosting fee + revenue share for distribution through third-party marketplaces. We can sketch options once legal aligns on CLA redlines.

Cc'ing Marissa and Priyom — Marissa for partner commercial terms and pricing, Priyom for model-onboarding requirements and the technical checklist.

Next step: would ScaleFabric be ok to propose redlines to the OW-CLA and for Redwood legal to reciprocate? If so we can follow a redline exchange cadence (3 business days each). I also attached a preliminary Hosting SLA (Redwood-Hosting-SLA-v1.pdf) with target SLOs and boundary conditions.

Cheers,
Karthik
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Hosting-SLA-v1.pdf

From: ScaleFabric Ltd (legal) <legal@scalefabric.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Dr. Lena Voss <lena@openweights.org>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Potential hosting & distribution terms for OpenWeights models

Karthik / Marissa —

Our legal team reviewed OW-CLA-draft and had three immediate redline topics:
1) Liability cap and indemnity carveouts for IP claims tied to upstream training data content. We propose a mutual cap equal to 12 months of hosting fees for initial pilots; higher for enterprise commitments.
2) Clarification on the "no-retraining-for-proprietary-derivatives" clause: we want explicit language allowing customer-managed fine-tuning if the customer owns resultant checkpoints and agrees to indemnify OpenWeights for any misuse. Redwood would keep an auditable record of derivative checkpoints and retention policy.
3) Export control / sanctions clause: need to ensure hosting doesn't put Redwood or the Consortium in breach; propose standard geographic and list-based compliance carveouts.

On the SLA: the SLOs look reasonable for Dedicated and Hosted tiers. We suggest adding an optional burst-tier pricing line and a black-box test plan for model integrity checks prior to onboarding.

If OW is comfortable, our suggestion is a redline exchange by Wed EOD (ScaleFabric) and Redwood to respond by Mon next week. Please advise.

Regards,
Martin K. (ScaleFabric Legal Counsel)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Dr. Lena Voss <lena@openweights.org>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential hosting & distribution terms for OpenWeights models

Lena / team —

Thanks for the draft and the fast replies. Quick commercial notes from Redwood:
- Pilot: propose a 90-day technical pilot (no revenue share) where Redwood will host up to 3 OW models (up to 1B params each or equivalent quantized footprint) for community and developer access. Pilot will include monthly usage reporting and a security questionnaire scope (SOC 2 in progress).
- Post-pilot options: (A) fixed hosting fee + market-rate revenue share for marketplace distribution, or (B) joint go-to-market with revenue split on enterprise deals. We can propose numbers after we see usage shape.
- Technical onboarding: Priyom, can you confirm the model packaging expectations (HF format + provenance JSON + license text) and the integrity checksum process? We also want a simple allowlist approach for customers who want to opt into fine-tuning so we don't violate the CLA.

Action items:
1) ScaleFabric to send redlines by Wed EOD (we'll review and send counters).
2) Priyom to publish the onboarding checklist to the shared Drive folder.
3) Karthik / Marissa to sync with Product on burst-tier pricing by next Wed.

Happy to hop on a short call if OW wants to walk through the redlines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference
